- **What we claim versus what we verified.** For every coverage claim the platform makes — key present, domain assigned, full-not-sampled, modeled — what share is value-verified versus merely asserted, and how many sources sit on the top rungs that could carry a published accusation? — CATALOG + COLUMN_CATALOG + CONNECT_EDGES provisional flags, sample flags, trust layers. *Harm:* publishing on unverified claims is how a platform loses the right to be believed; the honest size of Ripple is the curated, verified, fresh core — not the headline source count. · caveat: verification status is scattered across several fields and needs manual mapping; upper rungs are not a single stored field.
- **The honest time window for cross-source claims.** For which years do the most sources hold data simultaneously — the only period a cross-source finding can honestly cover? — CATALOG temporal coverage and data-through fields. *Harm:* claiming a cross-source pattern outside the shared window claims something the data cannot support. · caveat: temporal coverage is free text and start dates are not measured anywhere.
- **URL rot in the registry.** What share of registered source URLs are dead — leaving our copy as the only public copy, unaudited? — CATALOG URLs (requires live link-checking). *Harm:* when the original link dies our copy becomes the only public copy, and nobody audits us. · caveat: needs live fetching — a proposed measurement, not a query over held data.
- **How stale is the offshore record.** How much of the leak corpus is past its validity date, never records an end date, or shows struck-off entities still carrying live relationships — where can the record no longer be trusted? — ICIJ validity/note fields across addresses, officers, others, relationships (fed_icij_offshoreleaks_*). *Harm:* knowing the record's expiry date is how you avoid accusing someone on a decade-old fact. · medium · caveat: valid_until is a provenance note string, likely unparseable as a date; missing end dates may mean unknown, not still-active.
- **Series that start and stop with administrations.** For every enforcement-flavored source in the warehouse, plot record counts by action year — which enforcement streams visibly throttle up or down at administration changes, and which went quiet and never came back? — all enforcement/action-dated sources (EPA formal/informal actions, MSHA violations, OSHA, SDWA enforcement, FDIC/NCUA actions, SEC, etc.). *Harm:* enforcement that quietly stops is deregulation nobody voted on; the timestamp pattern is the evidence. · caveat: must first separate real slowdowns from load-window artifacts — completeness unverified on 376/558 sources makes this a two-step check.
- **The dark half of the map.** Which of the warehouse's biggest, most harm-relevant sources have ZERO verified connections in the entity graph — and what single crosswalk would light each one up? Confirmed dark today: DEA ARCOS 178M, PPP loans, OFAC/OpenSanctions/UN/EU/UK sanctions, ICIJ Offshore Leaks, ICE detention, MAUDE, NPDB, EOIR, CPSC injuries, FBI crime data, NHTSA, Senate lobbying, CourtListener judges. — connection graph vs the modeled catalog (outputs/connect_graph.json, CATALOG). *Harm:* the harm-heaviest datasets (opioids, sanctions, detention, device injuries) are exactly the ones the map cannot yet reach — the platform's own blind spot, measurable and rankable.
- **The regulators you cannot audit.** 376 of 558 sources have no publisher total to check completeness against — grouped by agency, which regulators publish data with no manifest, no row counts, no way for anyone to know if the public copy is whole? — modeled catalog plus the completeness-audit results (CATALOG). *Harm:* an unverifiable register can silently lose the worst records and no one can prove it.
- **Immigration court: 12.6M rows, one usable column.** The immigration court records table is a husk — quantify precisely what the public immigration-court record should contain versus what survived the load, and what questions (judge grant-rate disparity, representation effects, detention outcomes) are unaskable until reload. — EOIR case data (fed_eoir_case_data). *Harm:* asylum seekers' life-or-death odds vary enormously by judge — and the dataset that would prove it is currently unreadable. · caveat: the table is nearly unusable until reloaded — this question is about that fact.
- **The influence record is the least complete record.** Compare load completeness across the influence-industry sources — Senate lobbying at ~9%, Federal Register at ~9%, FARA small, Senate stock trades ending Dec 2020: is the money-and-influence corner of the warehouse systematically the thinnest, and is that itself a story about how influence data gets published? — Senate LDA filings, Federal Register, FARA, Senate stock watcher (fed_senate_lda_filings, fed_federal_register_documents, fed_fara_bulk, fed_senate_stock_watcher). *Harm:* the public's window into paid influence is the dirtiest glass in the building — partly the platform's loads, partly how the record is published. · medium · caveat: Senate lobbying ~9% loaded; Federal Register ~9%; Senate trades name-only and end Dec 2020.
- **Sanctions lists that touch nothing.** Every sanctions and screening list held (OFAC SDN, OpenSanctions, UN, EU, UK, consolidated screening list, FHFA suspended counterparties) has zero verified joins to the rest of the map — what one crosswalk (LEI for entities, then name+country with review for the rest) unlocks "sanctioned but still transacting" across contracts, shipping, and corporate registries? — the sanctions sources against the connection graph (fed_ofac_sdn, intl_opensanctions, xc_un_consolidated_sanctions_list, intl_eu_sanctions, xc_uk_sanctions_list, fed_consolidated_screening_list, fed_fhfa_suspended_counterparties). *Harm:* until connected, the platform structurally cannot see a sanctioned actor operating through a US-registered entity — the exact harm sanctions data exists to expose. · caveat: sentinel-masked IDs are the known trap on any future sanctions crosswalk — every candidate key needs COUNT(DISTINCT)+sample before trust.


---

# TIER 2 — two sources joined (475 questions: 57 SOLID / 418 FUZZY)

Connection questions: does X follow Y, who appears in both, what changes when you normalize A by B.

### health-and-medicine (85)
- **The counties that got the pills but never the treatment.** Which counties absorbed the historic pill flood and still have no opioid treatment program within reach?
  *Join:* ARCOS volumes (fed_dea_arcos_full) ↔ treatment program sites (fed_cms_opioid_treatment_program_providers) on ZIP→county — **FUZZY** (fix: build the ZIP-to-county crosswalk; verify treatment-program ZIP quality). *Harm:* The counties flooded with pills and left with no methadone clinic are where dependence became death. · caveat: treatment file has sites only, no capacity; death rates banded.
- **Supply that outruns any legitimate demand.** In which counties did pharmacies receive far more opioids than local prescribing could explain — the arithmetic signature of diversion?
  *Join:* ARCOS pharmacy receipts (fed_dea_arcos) ↔ Part D claims by prescriber county (fed_cms_part_d_prescribers) on county — **FUZZY** (fix: normalize county coding; state the Medicare-only denominator honestly or add another prescribing source). *Harm:* Diversion happens where supply exceeds any legitimate local demand, and neighborhoods pay for it. · caveat: Part D understates total prescribing.
- **Dying in the weeks after release.** Do state overdose death series spike in proportion to jail discharge volumes — the shape of the post-release death spike?
  *Join:* CDC monthly overdose (fed_cdc_overdose) ↔ jail discharges (xc_vera_incarceration_trends) on state — **FUZZY** (fix: state grain supports motivation only; the individual-level claim needs data the platform does not hold). *Harm:* People die in the first two weeks after release; the data can show the shape of it. · medium · caveat: annual discharge counts against monthly deaths — crude alignment.
- **What it costs versus what gets prescribed and paid.** How big is the markup between pharmacy acquisition cost and what Medicare pays per claim, and who keeps prescribing the brand where a cheap generic exists, weighted by the price gap?
  *Join:* NADAC (fed_cms_nadac) ↔ Part D drug rows (FED_CMS_PARTD_PRESCRIBER_DRUG) on drug name/NDC — **FUZZY** (fix: build and measure a drug-name-to-NDC bridge; promote it to the map if precision holds). *Harm:* The gap between what a pill costs and what the program pays is money that could have been care. · caveat: NADAC is pharmacy acquisition, not patient cost; Part D single-year snapshot.
- **Recalled drugs still being dispensed.** After a drug recall, how much Part D dispensing of that product continued?
  *Join:* FDA drug recalls (FED_FDA_DRUG_ENFORCEMENT) ↔ Part D (FED_CMS_PARTD_PRESCRIBER_DRUG) + NADAC on drug name / packed NDC lists — **FUZZY** (fix: parse and explode the NDC lists, verify format alignment, then measure the join). *Harm:* Patients still filling a recalled prescription are exposed to a product the maker already admitted was unsafe. · caveat: single Part D snapshot year may make the after-recall window impossible.
- **When a recall kills the cheap generic.** How much of recall volume hits cheap generics — recalls that vanish quietly while the patients relying on that supply lose it?
  *Join:* FDA drug recalls ↔ NADAC on NDC (packed multi-value recall field) — **FUZZY** (fix: explode and normalize the NDC list, then measure match rates). *Harm:* Recalls that hit cheap generics disappear quietly while patients lose supply. · medium
- **Recalled here, still sold there.** For active ingredients recalled in the US, does the same ingredient remain marketed in Canada — safety decisions that do not travel?
  *Join:* FDA drug recalls ↔ Health Canada registry (intl_healthcanada_dpd_drug) on ingredient name — **FUZZY** (fix: route both sides through the substance registry (UNII/CAS) instead of raw names). *Harm:* A safety decision in one country does not travel; patients across the border keep taking the product. · medium · caveat: Canadian mart has a known positional-rename loader defect — columns unverified.
- **The label changed before the recall did.** For drugs later recalled, did the label quietly change first — warning amended instead of product pulled?
  *Join:* DailyMed label versions (fed_nlm_dailymed_spl_setid_map) ↔ drug recalls on NDC/SPL set id — **FUZZY** (fix: verify whether label version history is capturable; build the NDC bridge). *Harm:* Manufacturers can amend the warning label instead of pulling the product — patients keep taking it. · medium · caveat: label mart may hold only current versions.
- **Does the clearance shortcut produce more harm?** Do 510(k)-cleared and lower-risk-class devices generate more recalls and adverse events than fully-approved (PMA) devices?
  *Join:* 510(k)/PMA/classification (FED_FDA_DEVICE_*) ↔ recalls (FED_FDA_DEVICE_ENFORCEMENT) ↔ adverse events (FED_FDA_MAUDE) on FDA product code, K-number where present — **FUZZY** (fix: measure product-code join precision across the FDA family and promote it into the connection map). *Harm:* If the fast pathway recalls and injures more, the shortcut is being paid for in patient injuries. · caveat: MAUDE load partial (2.7M of 25.7M, 2020Q1+); no in-use denominator — raw counts favor common devices.
- **The injuries came before the recall.** For each recalled device, how many injury and death reports had already accumulated before the recall date?
  *Join:* MAUDE ↔ device recalls on product code with recall date as marker — **FUZZY** (fix: measure product-code fill and join precision, then promote). *Harm:* Every death report before the recall date is a person the system already had evidence about. · caveat: MAUDE is 2020Q1+ only — earlier recalls falsely show an empty pre-period.
- **Recalls traced to the physical plant.** Which registered manufacturing plants — including foreign ones — generate the most recalls?
  *Join:* device recalls (FEI stored as comma-joined lists) ↔ establishment registrations (FED_FDA_ESTABLISHMENT_REG) on FEI — **FUZZY** (fix: split the list column, verify FEI fill on both sides, measure the join). *Harm:* Naming the plant rather than the brand finds the facility that keeps shipping defective devices.
- **Recalled but still listed as distributed.** Which device identifiers stay marked "in commercial distribution" after a life-threatening recall in the same product code?
  *Join:* GUDID (FED_FDA_GUDID) ↔ device recalls on product code — **FUZZY** (fix: verify whether recall records carry device identifiers that allow an exact match — product code is a category, not a device). *Harm:* A recalled device still listed as in distribution may still reach a patient.
- **Implants ranked by injury reports.** Which implantable categories generate the most adverse events per marketed device?
  *Join:* GUDID categories ↔ MAUDE on device identifier / product code — **FUZZY** (fix: profile UDI fill in MAUDE; fall back to product code and measure precision). *Harm:* Patients carrying implants have no public ranking of which ones fail. · medium · caveat: MAUDE load partial.
- **Cosmetics harm with no recall lever.** Cosmetic injury reports keep flowing while formal enforcement in the same categories sits near zero — how big is the enforcement vacuum?
  *Join:* CAERS (FED_FDA_CAERS) ↔ FDA enforcement — parallel comparison by category/period, no row-level join — **FUZZY** (fix: none available in-data; honest framing as parallel series is the method). *Harm:* Cosmetics injure people in a regulatory regime with almost no recall power. · medium · caveat: CAERS columns unverified.
- **Who bears drug harm — and who dies of it.** Which age and sex groups carry the fatal end of drug harm, not just the reports?
  *Join:* FAERS demographics (fed_fda_faers_demo) ↔ outcomes (fed_fda_faers_outc) on case id (primaryid/caseid) — **FUZZY** (fix: reconcile the two id eras, dedupe cases across quarterly drops, then promote the case-id join). *Harm:* Shows precisely which patients bear the fatal end of drug harm. · caveat: age needs normalization across unit codes or the distribution is meaningless.
- **Which drugs are actually most dangerous.** Ranked by death share and disproportionality — not raw report counts — which drugs top the danger list before regulators act?
  *Join:* FAERS drug ↔ outcomes ↔ reactions on case id — **FUZZY** (fix: dedupe case ids across eras/quarters; normalize drug names against a dictionary). *Harm:* Ranks by lethality rather than popularity — the number patients actually need. · caveat: denominators are reports, not prescriptions; disproportionality is easy to misread as causation.
- **The supplier behind the harmed patients.** Can a patient's injury be traced back through the drug to the ingredient supplier and its factory?
  *Join:* FAERS drug names (fed_fda_faers_drug) ↔ drug master files (fed_fda_drug_master_files) on subject text — **FUZZY** (fix: route both through the substance registry (UNII) as the bridge; measure match rates before believing anything). *Harm:* Connects a patient's injury to the offshore factory that made the ingredient. · wild
- **Did biosimilar entry ever lower the price?** For each reference biologic, what happened to its acquisition price after biosimilar approval?
  *Join:* Purple Book (FED_FDA_PURPLE_BOOK) ↔ NADAC on product name/NDC — **FUZZY** (fix: build a biologic name-to-NDC bridge and measure it). *Harm:* Patients never see the savings biosimilar approval was supposed to deliver. · caveat: Purple Book columns unverified.
- **Listed carcinogens inside approved products.** How many substances in approved drugs and foods match chemicals California lists as carcinogens or reproductive toxicants?
  *Join:* FDA substance registry (FED_FDA_UNII_GSRS_SUBSTANCES) ↔ Prop 65 (st_oehha_proposition_65_list) on CAS/UNII — **FUZZY** (fix: COUNT(DISTINCT) + value-sample CAS on both sides, measure precision, promote the edge). *Harm:* Substances a state calls carcinogenic are inside products people take daily. · medium · caveat: a listing does not mean the in-product exposure level is harmful — dose matters and the data cannot show it.
- **Marketing spend defends the price gap.** Does industry marketing money concentrate on exactly the drugs with the biggest brand-to-generic price ratios?
  *Join:* Open Payments drug-associated payments ↔ NADAC ratios on NDC / drug name — **FUZZY** (fix: profile NDC fill in Open Payments; fall back to a measured name bridge). *Harm:* Patients and Medicaid pay the brand premium the marketing spend defends.
- **The trial investigators on the sponsor's payroll.** What share of a sponsor's trial investigators also receive personal payments from that sponsor, and how large are they?
  *Join:* ClinicalTrials (fed_clinicaltrials) ↔ Open Payments on investigator NPI — **FUZZY** (fix: reload the full trial registry; profile investigator-NPI fill before joining). *Harm:* The evidence base doctors rely on is produced by people the maker pays. · caveat: trials mart is a 500-row stub.
- **Outside the program, still steering its money.** How many providers who opted out of Medicare remain on the ordering-and-referring roster?
  *Join:* opt-out affidavits (fed_cms_opt_out_affidavits) ↔ roster (fed_cms_order_and_referring) on NPI — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Providers outside the program still directing its money is the gap where equipment and hospice fraud lives. · caveat: NPI text formats may differ; the overlap may be small.
- **Excluded operators still running and staffing care.** Which hospitals, nursing homes, home-health agencies and hospices are affiliated with excluded clinicians or run by operators matching the federal ban lists?
  *Join:* LEIE / SAM exclusions ↔ facility affiliations and operator names on NPI (clinician hop) + name (operator hop) — **FUZZY** (fix: quantify NPI fill on both ban lists; entity-resolve operator names before any claim). *Harm:* Families walking into a facility cannot know it staffs or is run by banned operators. · caveat: affiliation snapshots carry no dates — currency at exclusion time unprovable.
- **Industry money and the excluded.** Did industry payments to later-excluded providers climb before their exclusion — and did manufacturers keep paying them while excluded?
  *Join:* Open Payments ↔ OIG LEIE on NPI — **SOLID**. *Harm:* If money is an early warning of misconduct, patients were harmed while the signal sat in public data. · caveat: LEIE NPI sparsity shrinks the matched set — bias must be stated; many exclusions are unrelated to prescribing.
- **License stripped in one state, billing in another.** Do state licensure actions fail to become federal exclusions — a gap that lets a stripped clinician keep billing elsewhere?
  *Join:* NPDB adverse actions (fed_hrsa_npdb) ↔ LEIE on state+year aggregates (NPDB is de-identified) — **FUZZY** (fix: none within held data — the person-level question is unanswerable; frame as state-level divergence only). *Harm:* A clinician stripped of a license in one state keeps billing federal programs elsewhere. · caveat: NPDB masks low-count states.
- **Harm found, dollars charged: the nursing home enforcement gap.** Facility by facility, how do harm-level citations compare with fines — and how many homes harm repeatedly while paying nothing?
  *Join:* deficiencies (fed_cms_nursing_home_deficiencies) ↔ penalties (fed_cms_nursing_home_penalties) on CCN — **SOLID**. *Harm:* When the fine is smaller than a week of profit, a resident's harm is priced as a cost of business. · caveat: penalty file may be a rolling window while deficiencies go back further — a zero fine could mean out-of-window; fine amounts may be text.
- **Roll the record up to the owner.** Which corporate owners produce harm across their whole nursing-home portfolio when citations, fines and abuse findings are rolled up from facilities?
  *Join:* deficiencies/penalties on CCN, then facility → affiliation_entity_id / chain name — **FUZZY** (fix: COUNT(DISTINCT) + value-sample the affiliation id; entity-resolve chain names; promote the owner key if it holds). *Harm:* A chain that treats fines as overhead spreads the same neglect across every home it owns. · caveat: CCN formats may differ between tables.
- **Margin up, staffing down.** Which nursing home operators post improving margins while their nurse hours per resident fall?
  *Join:* HCRIS cost reports (fed_cms_hcris) ↔ staffing (fed_nursinghome411) on CCN — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Residents lose bedside hours in exactly the facilities posting the best financials. · caveat: HCRIS is hospital-heavy — skilled-nursing coverage unverified, may be thin.
- **Sedated instead of staffed.** Do facilities with high antipsychotic/chemical-restraint measures also carry abuse and neglect citations?
  *Join:* facility MDS measures (fed_cms_facility_level_minimum_data_set_frequency) ↔ deficiency tags on CCN — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Residents may be sedated instead of staffed — and the citation record would show it. · caveat: identifying the right MDS items is free-text-dependent; 31M-row grain unverified.
- **Bad homes in counties with no alternative.** Which counties are both provider-shortage areas and full of harm-cited nursing homes?
  *Join:* deficiencies ↔ HRSA shortage areas (fed_hrsa_shortage_areas) on facility ZIP→county — **FUZZY** (fix: build/verify the ZIP-to-county crosswalk; sub-county HPSA components complicate the rollup). *Harm:* Families in shortage counties cannot move a relative out of a bad home because there is nowhere else to go.
- **Two records, one nursing home.** Where do CMS's published numbers and the LTCCC compilation disagree on the same facility?
  *Join:* CMS compare (fed_cms_nursing_home) ↔ LTCCC (fed_nursinghome411) on CCN — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Where the public records disagree, a family reading one of them is being misled. · medium · caveat: LTCCC compiles from CMS — the interest is entirely in the exceptions.
- **What the nonprofit hospital deal actually buys.** Do tax-exempt hospitals deliver what the exemption pays for — executive pay, asset size, charity care, quality — across the same hospitals?
  *Join:* HCRIS + hospital quality on CCN (solid legs); IRS BMF / 990 index via name→EIN — **FUZZY** (fix: land the 990 filing data and build a measured EIN-to-CCN crosswalk). *Harm:* Communities give the tax break and may get worse care and no charity — while patients get sued for bills. · medium · caveat: 990 mart is index-only, compensation may be blocked until filings land; fiscal years misalign with quality snapshots.
- **Hospitals failing their audits and their patients.** Do hospitals with adverse federal single-audit findings also show worse patient safety and mortality?
  *Join:* single audits (FED_FAC_SINGLE_AUDIT) ↔ hospital quality (fed_cms_hospital_general) via name→EIN — **FUZZY** (fix: build the EIN-CCN crosswalk; audit field names unverified). *Harm:* Hospitals that cannot manage their federal money may not be managing their patients either. · medium
- **Service lines quietly closed.** Which hospitals dropped obstetrics, psychiatric units, or emergency services between snapshots?
  *Join:* hospital service/unit flags across snapshots (fed_cms_hospital_general, fed_cms_pos_other) on CCN — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Whole counties lose the ability to deliver a baby or handle a crisis, and nobody announces it. · caveat: services file may be a single snapshot — check for multiple vintages first.
- **New agencies flocking to weak oversight.** Do new home-health agencies cluster in counties where existing agencies already rate poorly?
  *Join:* HH enrollments (fed_cms_home_health_agency_enrollments) ↔ HH quality (fed_cms_home_health) on CCN — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Fly-by-night agencies open where nobody is checking, and homebound patients get whoever shows up. · medium · caveat: enrollment-date and quality-rating columns unverified.
- **Hospice churn: dying patients changing hands.** How often are hospices enrolled, terminated, and traded between owners?
  *Join:* hospice facility file (fed_cms_hospice) ↔ hospice enrollments on CCN — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Dying patients are handed between operators chasing the reimbursement. · medium · caveat: termination and ownership-change fields unverified.
- **Where medical debt piles up.** Do medical-debt complaints cluster around particular hospital markets and ownership types, and does coverage loss show up months later as collections complaints?
  *Join:* CFPB complaints (FED_CFPB_COMPLAINTS) ↔ hospital ownership ↔ uninsured rates on ZIP/state — **FUZZY** (fix: define the medical-debt tag transparently; accept ZIP3 grain — complaint ZIPs are truncated). *Harm:* Patients in some hospital markets end up in collections far more often; losing coverage becomes debt months later. · caveat: complaint volume reflects who knows how to complain — biased toward better-off areas.
- **Coverage loss and distress, same people, same months.** Do the groups losing insurance coverage also report rising anxiety and depression at the same time?
  *Join:* Pulse uninsured (fed_cdc_health_insurance) ↔ Pulse anxiety/depression (fed_cdc_anxiety_depression) on state+subgroup+period — **FUZZY** (fix: verify the subgroup/period vocabularies align exactly — then effectively clean, though not an entity-graph edge). *Harm:* Groups losing coverage and reporting rising distress at once are the ones with nowhere to go. · caveat: suppression and wide CIs on small subgroups can manufacture apparent correlation.
- **Does the shortage designation follow the need?** When reported mental distress rises in a state, do mental-health shortage designations follow?
  *Join:* Pulse distress ↔ HRSA designations (fed_hrsa_shortage_areas) on state — **FUZZY** (fix: verify state coding; accept the coarse grain). *Harm:* Need rises and the paperwork that unlocks help never moves. · caveat: self-reported, pandemic-era heavy; designations slow-moving by design.
- **Is the official shortage map just wrong?** Which designated areas are actually fine, and which undesignated deserts get no federal help because the designation missed them?
  *Join:* NPPES provider counts + billing locations ↔ HPSA designations (fed_hrsa_shortage_areas, fed_hrsa_hpsa_primary_care) on county FIPS via ZIP crosswalk — **FUZZY** (fix: build the crosswalk; use billing files, not registration, as the activity signal). *Harm:* If the map is wrong, the funding that follows it goes to the wrong places and real shortages stay unfunded.
- **Shortage areas draining faster.** Are providers deactivating out of designated shortage ZIPs faster than elsewhere?
  *Join:* NPPES deactivation (fed_cms_nppes) ↔ shortage designations on ZIP — **FUZZY** (fix: profile deactivation-date fill; NPPES is a snapshot — churn needs archived vintages). *Harm:* Shortage areas get thinner every year while the designation stays static. · medium
- **Severe shortage, zero safety-net clinics.** Which high-severity shortage counties have no safety-net clinic site at all?
  *Join:* HPSA (fed_hrsa_hpsa_primary_care) ↔ UDS delivery sites (fed_hrsa_uds_service_delivery_sites) on county FIPS — **FUZZY** (fix: test the shared organization-id join both tables carry — it may upgrade this; verify FIPS formatting). *Harm:* A county with a severe doctor shortage and zero safety-net clinics is a place where poor people simply do not get care.
- **Outbreaks where there is no clinic.** Where are notifiable diseases surging in places with no safety-net clinic coverage?
  *Join:* NNDSS (fed_cdc_nndss_weekly_2024) ↔ FQHC enrollments (fed_cms_federally_qualified_health_center_enrollments) on state/county geography — **FUZZY** (fix: restrict to the jurisdictions where NNDSS reports below state level). *Harm:* Disease surging where there is no clinic means the sick have nowhere to go. · medium
- **Citations after the outbreak, not before.** Do infection-control citations in nursing homes follow disease waves rather than precede them?
  *Join:* infection-control deficiencies ↔ NNDSS weekly counts on state+week — **FUZZY** (fix: none fully — survey scheduling confounds citation timing by design; frame honestly). *Harm:* Homes get cited only after residents are already sick. · medium · caveat: survey scheduling drives citation timing more than outbreaks — confounded.
- **Hurt most where treatment is least.** Which high-injury counties have no trauma or emergency capacity?
  *Join:* facility services (fed_cms_pos_other) ↔ CDC injury rates (fed_cdc_injury_violence_county) on county FIPS — **FUZZY** (fix: decode the facility service codes; verify facility county fields). *Harm:* People are injured most in the counties with the least ability to treat them. · caveat: facility snapshot date unknown.
- **Dialysis chairs on a failing grid.** Which dialysis facilities sit inside the utility territories with the worst outage records?
  *Join:* EIA-861 reliability (FED_EIA861_RELIABILITY) ↔ dialysis locations (fed_cms_dialysis) on service-territory geography — **FUZZY** (fix: land/verify service-territory geography; assign facilities by location). *Harm:* Dialysis patients in weak-grid areas miss treatment when the power fails — a life-threatening event.
- **Veteran deaths and the hospitals around them.** Do states with weaker hospitals show higher veteran mortality — and does veteran suicide track states where mental-health care is formally declared insufficient?
  *Join:* VA mortality/suicide (fed_va_allcause_mortality, fed_va_suicide_state) ↔ hospital quality ↔ shortage coverage on state — **FUZZY** (fix: accept the grain; veterans often use VA facilities not in the hospital file — say so). *Harm:* Where a veteran lives changes their odds. · caveat: VA columns partially unverified; designation is a policy artifact, not a direct access measure.
- **Trained here, gone tomorrow.** Which states train health workers and then lose them — net importers and exporters of clinicians?
  *Join:* College Scorecard health programs (fed_ed_college_scorecard_institution) ↔ NPPES enrollment states on state aggregates — **FUZZY** (fix: none in held data — no person-level link; frame strictly as aggregate correlation). *Harm:* States that train clinicians and lose them all stay short of care. · wild
- **Who is re-entering the Medicare queue.** Are pending enrollment applicants new clinicians or providers cycling back in — including some previously opted out or removed?
  *Join:* pending queues (fed_cms_pending_initial_logging_and_tracking_*) ↔ active enrollment ↔ opt-outs on NPI — **FUZZY** (fix: COUNT(DISTINCT) NPI in the thin queue tables first — key population unverified). *Harm:* Re-applicants may be providers previously removed, quietly coming back in. · wild · caveat: the overlap may be near zero.
- **The exclusion-to-deactivation lag.** After a provider is federally excluded, how long until their NPI is actually deactivated in the national registry — if ever?
  *Join:* LEIE dates ↔ NPPES deactivation dates on NPI — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Every month between ban and deactivation is a month the billing system cannot see the ban. · caveat: LEIE NPI sparsity and NPPES deactivation-field fill must both be profiled first.
- **Does the record reset when the home is sold?** After a nursing home changes ownership, do its fines and citations drop — because enforcement effectively restarts against the new owner?
  *Join:* ownership-change flags (fed_cms_nursing_home) ↔ penalty/deficiency timelines on CCN with the change window as event marker — **SOLID**. *Harm:* If a sale wipes the enforcement slate, flipping homes becomes a laundering mechanism for bad operators. · caveat: ownership-change flag is a 12-month snapshot — event timing approximate.
- **Displaced abortion demand meets fixed maternity capacity.** In the states absorbing displaced abortion patients, how does surging demand compare with existing obstetric and birthing-friendly capacity?
  *Join:* Guttmacher provision surges (xc_guttmacher_monthly_abortion) ↔ hospital obstetric flags (fed_cms_hospital_compare, fed_cms_pos_other) on state — **FUZZY** (fix: verify obstetric service flags decode correctly; accept coarse grain). *Harm:* Receiving-state waiting lists push everyone's care — including residents' — later into pregnancy. · medium
- **Royalty doctors and the devices that fail.** Which physicians receive royalty payments from device makers whose devices carry heavy injury reports?
  *Join:* Open Payments royalty payments ↔ MAUDE on manufacturer/device name — **FUZZY** (fix: build the manufacturer name bridge; the royalty subset is small enough to curate). *Harm:* A surgeon paid royalties on the implant chooses it for patients who never see the royalty. · medium · caveat: MAUDE load partial.
- **The label lag after the signal.** When an adverse-reaction signal spikes for a drug, how long before its label version actually changes?
  *Join:* FAERS signals (fed_fda_faers_reac, fed_fda_faers_drug) ↔ DailyMed versions on drug name→set id — **FUZZY** (fix: measured name bridge via label product names; current-versions-only storage means lag needs archived vintages). *Harm:* The months between a visible harm signal and the warning label are months of uninformed exposure. · medium
- **Marketing pressure where the doctor is the only one.** Is per-doctor industry marketing heavier or lighter in shortage areas?
  *Join:* Open Payments per-NPI intensity → provider ZIP (solid hops) → shortage designation — **FUZZY** (fix: verify ZIP-level HPSA assignment — the final hop is geographic). *Harm:* In a one-doctor county, one influenced prescriber is the whole standard of care. · wild
- **Do formation booms predict later enforcement?** Do boom-year hospice and home-health cohorts get terminated, excluded, or penalized at higher rates later?
  *Join:* enrollment formation cohorts ↔ terminations (fed_cms_pos_other) on CCN; exclusions via NPI/name — **FUZZY** (fix: verify CCN format alignment across the files; quantify the LEIE exclusion undercount). *Harm:* If boom cohorts predict enforcement, regulators could act at entry instead of after patients are harmed. · medium · caveat: incorporation-date parse quality unknown.
- **Which causes explain the American gap.** Decomposing the US life-expectancy shortfall against peer countries by cause of death: how much is overdose, guns, roads, and uninsured chronic disease?
  *Join:* OWID life expectancy (xc_owid_life_expectancy) ↔ US cause mix (fed_cdc_wonder, fed_cdc_leading_causes_state) on country/year alignment — **FUZZY** (fix: alignment is methodological (age-standardization), not a key problem; document it). *Harm:* Names which specific American policy failures buy the years of life lost. · medium · caveat: WONDER is national-grain only; leading-causes data ends 2017.
- **Who loses when the rural hospital converts.** In counties whose hospital converted to emergency-only status, what happened afterward to injury deaths, overdose deaths, and access — against the county's own baseline?
  *Join:* conversion flags/dates (fed_cms_hospital_enrollments) ↔ county injury/overdose rates on county FIPS with conversion date as event marker — **FUZZY** (fix: verify hospital county coding; CDC period grain decides feasibility). *Harm:* If deaths rise after conversions, the quiet removal of rural beds has a measurable body count. · medium · caveat: post-period may be short; CDC rates banded and suppressed in small counties.
- **Noncompliant plants in already-hurt counties.** Which counties carry both heavy noncompliant-facility burdens and the worst health-harm rates?
  *Join:* EPA ECHO (fed_epa_echo) ↔ CDC injury/violence county file on county FIPS — **FUZZY** (fix: swap in a pollution-linked health outcome source — the CDC file measures injury and violence, not pollution-caused illness). *Harm:* The same counties absorb both unchecked pollution and the worst health outcomes. · medium · caveat: correlation is not the mechanism.
- **Lead exposure mapped to real places.** Take each water system's worst lead samples and put them on the ZIPs and counties the system serves.
  *Join:* SDWA lead/copper samples (FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_LCR_SAMPLES) ↔ SDWA geographic areas on PWSID — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Turns an abstract system ID into the streets where the lead is. · caveat: one system serves many ZIPs — attribution approximate; sample measure uncast, units mixed.
- **People drinking water in violation.** Weight health-based violations by the population each system serves — how many actual humans, and how do school/daycare systems compare?
  *Join:* SDWA violations/enforcement ↔ public water systems (FED_EPA_SDWA_SDWA_PUB_WATER_SYSTEMS) on PWSID — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Millions of people drink from systems in ongoing health-based violation; the unit is people, not systems. · caveat: overlapping violation periods double-count; population-served staleness; school/daycare flag fill unverified.
- **Lead at the school tap.** What are the worst lead sample results specifically at systems flagged as serving schools and daycares?
  *Join:* SDWA lead samples ↔ systems school/daycare flag on PWSID — **SOLID**. *Harm:* Lead's worst victims are children — the most direct child-exposure question the warehouse can ask. · caveat: school/daycare flag fill unverified; sample units must be normalized.
- **Veteran suicide and gun access.** Does the state-level veteran suicide rate track handgun background-check volume per capita over time?
  *Join:* VA veteran suicide by state (fed_va_suicide_state) ↔ FBI NICS checks (fed_fbi_nics_checks) on state + year — **FUZZY** (fix: one-time state-name vocabulary check; state is not a hard key, and NICS-as-proxy must be stated openly). *Harm:* Means-of-death policy is a veterans' policy whether anyone admits it or not. · medium · caveat: NICS checks are not sales; state aggregation obscures individual access.
- **Mortality and the political map.** Do state death rates by cause diverge along the political map after major policy splits — is who runs your state deciding how long you live?
  *Join:* NCHS leading causes of death (fed_cdc_leading_causes_state) ↔ MEDSL presidential returns (fed_medsl_president_returns) on state + year — **FUZZY** (fix: the state join is mechanical but not a hard-ID edge; the claim needs confounder controls — age, income, rurality — before it is trustworthy). *Harm:* Where you live, and who runs it, may be deciding how long you live. · medium · caveat: correlational and politically charged; completeness unverified.
- **Excluded providers still in the Medicare stream.** Are providers on the HHS exclusion list still prescribing Part D drugs, on the order-and-referral roster, referring durable medical equipment, or billing Medicare after their exclusion date?
  *Join:* OIG exclusion list (FED_HHS_OIG_LEIE) ↔ Part D prescribers / order-and-referring / Medicare utilization (FED_CMS_*) on NPI — **SOLID** (edges verified; 243–509 excluded NPIs already matched in Part D). *Harm:* patients unknowingly treated by providers already judged too dangerous or fraudulent for Medicare. · caveat: LEIE NPI only ~10% populated — a match is real, a non-match proves nothing for pre-NPI exclusions; compare exclusion date vs activity year; the DME-supplier leg's NPI edge is not yet in the graph — measure it (small tables) before extending there.
- **Drug-maker money and the prescription needle.** For doctors who took industry payments, does Part D prescribing tilt toward the paying manufacturer's drugs versus unpaid same-specialty peers — and who takes the most money per prescription written?
  *Join:* CMS Open Payments (FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS*) ↔ Part D prescriber-by-drug (FED_CMS_PARTD_PRESCRIBER_DRUG) on NPI — **SOLID** (verified, 75% / 734,802 NPIs; drug-to-manufacturer is within-row in Open Payments). *Harm:* patients get the sponsored drug, not the best or cheapest one, and taxpayers fund the markup. · caveat: Open Payments split-by-year table trap; Part D detail is one data year (DY2022) — align years before any causal framing.
- **Industry money vs quality scores.** Do doctors taking the most industry money score better or worse on Medicare's own quality program than doctors who take none?
  *Join:* Open Payments ↔ Quality Payment Program experience file on NPI — **SOLID** (verified). *Harm:* patients of paid doctors may be getting a measurably worse deal without knowing it. · medium · caveat: split-year table trap; completeness unverified.
- **Industry money vs billing volume.** Do doctors who take industry payments bill Medicare for more services or costlier service mixes than unpaid peers of the same specialty?
  *Join:* Open Payments ↔ Medicare physician utilization by provider on NPI — **SOLID** (verified, 61.5% match). *Harm:* sponsorship-driven overtreatment costs patients copays and unneeded procedures. · medium · caveat: split-year trap; completeness unverified.
- **Doctors at the most-penalized nursing homes.** Which physicians practice at nursing homes that rack up the biggest fines and payment denials, and how concentrated is that affiliation?
  *Join:* CMS facility affiliations ↔ nursing home penalties on CCN — **SOLID** (verified, 90.3%). *Harm:* families choose doctors with no idea the doctor's facilities are serial fine-collectors. · medium · caveat: completeness unverified.
- **Staffing vs fines in nursing homes.** Do the thinnest-staffed homes rack up more fines and payment suspensions — and does the fine actually change staffing afterward?
  *Join:* Nursing Home Care Compare ↔ nursing home penalties on CCN — **SOLID** (verified). *Harm:* understaffed homes mean neglected residents; fines that change nothing are theater. · caveat: completeness unverified.
- **Deficiency files vs star ratings.** Do raw deficiency records (including fire-safety) contradict the star ratings families actually see when picking a home?
  *Join:* nursing home deficiencies + fire deficiencies ↔ Care Compare ratings on CCN — **SOLID** (verified, 100%). *Harm:* a high-star home with a thick deficiency file is a mislabel that costs residents their safety. · caveat: completeness unverified.
- **Ownership type vs care quality.** Do for-profit or chain-owned nursing homes and hospitals systematically score worse on quality, staffing, and deficiencies than nonprofit or independent ones?
  *Join:* SNF/hospital enrollments (ownership fields) ↔ Care Compare / Hospital Compare on CCN — **SOLID** (verified, 99.8% / 98%). *Harm:* if ownership structure predicts neglect, the harm is systemic and buyable. · caveat: completeness unverified.
- **Hospital margins vs care quality.** Do hospitals with the fattest margins in their own cost reports deliver better care, or do profits and quality run in opposite directions?
  *Join:* HCRIS cost reports ↔ Hospital Compare (+ inpatient charge data) on CCN — **SOLID** (verified). *Harm:* patients pay the highest prices at hospitals that may deliver the least. · medium · caveat: HCRIS covers hospitals only (confirmed — cannot extend to nursing homes); completeness unverified.
- **Pills shipped vs overdose deaths.** Do the places flooded with controlled-substance shipments die more, and with what lag?
  *Join:* DEA ARCOS distribution (FED_DEA_ARCOS_FULL, 178M rows) ↔ NCHS drug-poisoning mortality by county — **FUZZY** (fix: land a ZIP-to-county crosswalk and verify which ARCOS geography column is actually populated before aggregating). *Harm:* the opioid supply-to-death pipeline measured for every county, not the famous few. · caveat: completeness unverified both sides.
- **Care deserts and overdose mortality.** Do counties designated health-professional shortage areas show higher drug-poisoning death rates than similar covered counties?
  *Join:* HRSA shortage areas ↔ drug-poisoning mortality on county FIPS — **FUZZY** (fix: FIPS-on-FIPS is nearly deterministic — value-verify both FIPS columns and align vintage years). *Harm:* people in places without doctors die of treatable addiction. · medium · caveat: completeness unverified.
- **Pills per person, county by county.** Normalized by population, which counties received the most opioid pills per resident — and which distributors served them?
  *Join:* DEA ARCOS ↔ county population reference on county FIPS rollup — **FUZZY** (fix: ARCOS has zero verified graph edges — validate its county fields and land a proper population reference table; the DEA registrant-number columns could make the distributor leg hard-ID). *Harm:* raw counts hide small hard-hit places drowning in pills. · caveat: completeness unverified.
- **Dialysis duopoly towns.** In counties where one or two chains control all dialysis facilities, are quality measures and penalty rates worse than in contested markets?
  *Join:* CMS dialysis facility listing (chain fields) ↔ Medicare dialysis facility detail on CCN — **SOLID** (verified). *Harm:* dialysis patients can't shop — a captured market removes the only pressure toward keeping them alive longer. · medium · caveat: completeness unverified.
- **How long the FDA sits on a signal.** For drugs eventually recalled, how many adverse-event reports piled up between the first serious-outcome report and the recall — and which manufacturers show the longest lag?
  *Join:* FAERS adverse events ↔ FDA drug enforcement/recalls on drug name — **FUZZY** (fix: normalize both sides through the NDC/SPL name spine (DailyMed set-id map is held); verify per drug before naming anyone). *Harm:* every month of lag is measured in injured patients who reported and were not heard. · caveat: two FAERS component tables show blank row counts in the catalog — confirm load state first.

### courts-and-justice (57)
- **Violent death, by whose hand.** In the highest-violence counties, what share of violent deaths involve police — a share no official statistic reports?

### sanctions-and-enforcement (18)
- **The two federal ban lists that disagree.** How many parties are on the health exclusion list but not the federal debarment list (or vice versa) — and how many are still actively enumerated as providers?

- **Excluded operators still running detention.** Do any federally excluded entities match the operators behind immigration detention facilities?

- **State AGs fill the federal gap — or don't.** When federal consumer enforcement retreats, do multistate AG settlements rise to fill the gap — and in which years did nobody protect consumers at all?
  *Join:* FTC enforcement actions (fed_ftc_datasets) ↔ NAAG multistate settlements (fed_naag_multistate_settlements) on issue area + year — **FUZZY** (fix: the two issue taxonomies differ entirely — hand-map them and publish the mapping). *Harm:* When federal enforcement drops and state AGs do not fill it, consumers in those years have no protector at all. · caveat: FTC mart may be a partial scrape.
- **Penalties as rounding errors.** How large is each corporate settlement as a share of the company's reported assets — which penalties were too small to deter anything?
  *Join:* NAAG settlements (fed_naag_multistate_settlements) ↔ SEC EDGAR financials (fed_sec_edgar_financials) on defendant name → filer (CIK once matched) — **FUZZY** (fix: build a defendant-name resolver against the entity spine — once matched to CIK the financial side rides a hard ID). *Harm:* Penalties too small to deter mean the harm is simply a cost of doing business. · caveat: NAAG mart is a passthrough with unverified columns.
- **Sanctioned vessels in US waters.** Do ships on the SDN list show AIS tracks and port calls in US waters after their designation date?
  *Join:* OFAC SDN vessels (fed_ofac_sdn) ↔ NOAA AIS vessel tracks (fed_noaa_ais) on IMO number — **FUZZY** (fix: AIS imo_number was found ~56% sentinel-masked on this platform and the SDN IMO is derived — COUNT(DISTINCT) + value samples on both sides before trusting any match; IMO is not on the steel-key list). *Harm:* Sanctioned shipping moving cargo through US waters unchallenged. · caveat: SDN vessel IMO coverage is small.
- **Sanctioned names behind ordinary companies.** Do sanctioned people appear in the UK company register — as registered companies or persons with significant control — running ordinary-looking businesses with real bank accounts?

- **Transatlantic designation lag.** For targets on both the US and EU lists, how long is the gap between the US start date and the EU publication date — the window to move assets out of reach?

- **Settled but never suspended.** Do companies that settle False Claims Act fraud cases ever appear on the exclusion list — or does settling buy immunity from debarment?
  *Join:* DOJ FCA settlements (fed_doj_fca_settlements) ↔ SAM.gov exclusions (fed_sam_exclusions) on company name (UEI once resolved via the entity spine) — **FUZZY** (fix: both marts are partial — re-ingest first; today this is a method test, not a finding). *Harm:* If fraud settlements never trigger debarment, the penalty system has a designed-in escape hatch. · medium · caveat: FCA mart is 12 rows; exclusions mart partial.
- **Are the hospital-killers sanctioned.** Do the ransomware gangs hitting hospitals, schools, and utilities appear on any sanctions list — and how long after their first victims did designation come, if ever?

- **Pandemic loans to barred entities.** How many PPP loans went to borrowers matching an active federal exclusion at approval time — emergency money with no check against the government's own ban list?

- **Offshore-linked federal vendors.** Do any federal contract recipients or their parents match entities and officers in the offshore leaks — public money touching structures built for concealment?

- **Complaints that led nowhere.** Which companies generate the most consumer complaints without ever drawing an FTC enforcement action?
  *Join:* CFPB consumer complaints ↔ FTC enforcement actions on company name — **FUZZY** (fix: build a brand-to-legal-entity name bridge; complaint names are consumer-facing brands). *Harm:* most consumer harm generates paperwork and no consequence. · caveat: the FTC mart is 1,200 rows and name-only; completeness unverified.
- **Sanctioned names in the aircraft registry.** Do any FAA aircraft registrants, trustees, or co-owner names match sanctioned parties or their known aliases?
